taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): more or less glandular-pubescent herb 1-4 dm. tall.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): leaves crowded on a short caudex: a perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): a herb.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the leaves die back each winter under the snow.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): leaves mostly basal, crowded on a short caudex.

traits.cauline_leaves.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): flowering stems bearing bracts, usually much smaller than the leaves, only the lower often foliaceous: drawn leafless.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): leaves spatulate to oblanceolate-spatulate, 2-8 cm. long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 8 mm to 2.5 cm wide at the toothed tip, as in the photos.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): spatulate to oblanceolate-spatulate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): sharply and sometimes broadly toothed mostly above the middle.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): more or less pubescent.

traits.glandular_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): more or less glandular-pubescent herb.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): flowering stems solitary or several, rather widely paniculate, the branches ascending.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the open panicle 8 cm to 25 cm long, half or more of the stem, as in the photos.

traits.inflorescence_branches.note: 5 to 12 ascending side branches to a panicle, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 234901797, 118449153, 233235518, 89643556, 10114403, 294953244, 15319701, 1820994): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: 20 to 60 flowers to a panicle, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 234901797, 118449153, 233235518, 89643556, 10114403, 294953244, 15319701, 1820994): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: open flowers 8 mm to 11 mm across, about twice the 3.5-5 mm petals Abrams (1944 p. 361) gives.

traits.petal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): petals unequal, oblong-lanceolate to spatulate-elliptic, 3.5-5 mm. long.

traits.petal_shape.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): petals oblong-lanceolate to spatulate-elliptic; drawn spatulate, the three upper broad, as in the photos.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): petals unequal.

traits.sepal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): sepals oblong-ovate, 1-2.5 mm. long, reflexed.

traits.sepal_posture.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): sepals reflexed.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): petals white with 2 yellow spots at the base; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.anther_colour.note: Anthers orange; sRGB by eye, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 234901797, 118449153, 233235518, 89643556, 10114403, 294953244, 15319701, 1820994): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): carpels united for two-thirds of their lengths, the style-tips divergent; the family's capsule.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 361, Saxifraga ferruginea (now Micranthes ferruginea): July-Aug.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: capsules ripe August and September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a rosette of spoon-shaped leaves toothed toward the tip, sending up slender reddish, glandular stalks with an open, airy panicle of small white flowers with orange anthers. The basal leaves' petiole share is set by hand from the leaf and petiole lengths the traits give, as no rule sets a rosette leaf's.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for rusty saxifrage from its sources and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). Its inflorescence is drawn as one cluster at each stem's tip, sized by the traits, so the stem ends where the cluster begins. The rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.4 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
